checks.description: Observational: adopters retain much better than non-adopters at D90 (raw gap)
checks.sql: WITH ret AS ( SELECT u.user_id, u.prior_engagement_tier AS tier, u.engagement_style AS style, EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM fc_.events e WHERE e.user_id = u.user_id AND e.event_name = 'app_open' AND e.event_ts >= u.signup_ts + interval '90 days') AS retained FROM fc_.users u WHERE u.signup_ts < timestamptz '2026-07-01 00:00:00+00' ), ai AS ( SELECT DISTINCT user_id FROM fc_.events WHERE event_name = 'ai_coach_session' AND user_id NOT IN (SELECT user_id FROM fc_.experiment_assignments WHERE experiment_key = 'ai_coach_holdout_2026q1') ) SELECT (SELECT avg(retained::int) FROM ret WHERE user_id IN (SELECT user_id FROM ai)) - (SELECT avg(retained::int) FROM ret WHERE user_id NOT IN (SELECT user_id FROM ai))

checks.description: Power-user selection: adopters are over-represented in the high engagement tier (ratio vs population)
checks.sql: WITH ai AS (SELECT DISTINCT user_id FROM fc_.events WHERE event_name='ai_coach_session' AND user_id NOT IN (SELECT user_id FROM fc_.experiment_assignments WHERE experiment_key='ai_coach_holdout_2026q1')) SELECT (SELECT avg((prior_engagement_tier='high')::int) FROM fc_.users WHERE user_id IN (SELECT user_id FROM ai)) / (SELECT avg((prior_engagement_tier='high')::int) FROM fc_.users)

checks.description: Within engagement tiers the adopter gap is a small fraction of the raw gap (selection explains most of it)
checks.sql: WITH ret AS ( SELECT u.user_id, u.prior_engagement_tier AS tier, u.engagement_style AS style, EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM fc_.events e WHERE e.user_id = u.user_id AND e.event_name = 'app_open' AND e.event_ts >= u.signup_ts + interval '90 days') AS retained FROM fc_.users u WHERE u.signup_ts < timestamptz '2026-07-01 00:00:00+00' ), ai AS ( SELECT DISTINCT user_id FROM fc_.events WHERE event_name = 'ai_coach_session' AND user_id NOT IN (SELECT user_id FROM fc_.experiment_assignments WHERE experiment_key = 'ai_coach_holdout_2026q1') ), t AS (SELECT tier, (user_id IN (SELECT user_id FROM ai)) AS adopter, avg(retained::int) AS r, count(*) AS n FROM ret GROUP BY 1, 2), g AS (SELECT a.n AS n_adopt, a.r - b.r AS gap FROM t a JOIN t b ON a.tier = b.tier AND a.adopter AND NOT b.adopter), raw AS (SELECT (SELECT avg(retained::int) FROM ret WHERE user_id IN (SELECT user_id FROM ai)) - (SELECT avg(retained::int) FROM ret WHERE user_id NOT IN (SELECT user_id FROM ai)) AS gap) SELECT (SELECT sum(n_adopt * gap) / sum(n_adopt) FROM g) / (SELECT gap FROM raw)

ai_coach.decision: Invest in expanding the AI Coach
patterns: power-user selection effect (adoption concentrated in the high engagement tier)
high inference cost per active adopter-month
weak, imbalanced (30/70 vs planned 50/50), short (14 day) experiment with contamination
composition-driven aggregate: joiners are mostly the high-baseline segment
aggregate-vs-segment heterogeneity / aggregate masking: the positive aggregate conceals an about-zero effect in segment B and a negative effect in segment C (together about 70% of users)
community.terminology_note: Related to Simpson-type aggregation risks, but this is not a textbook Simpson's paradox: the aggregate is positive and segment effects are mixed, not all reversed.
